summary.text: A 25-year old Caucasian woman with well-controlled Crohn disease on infliximab and a vegan diet presented to a surgical outpatient facility with right lower quadrant abdominal pain. Two weeks earlier she had gone to the emergency room with fever, chills, abdominal pain and diarrhea, and CT showed a right lower quadrant psoas abscess posterior to the cecum that was attributed to perforated appendicitis.

She had CT-guided drainage, cultures positive for S. intermedius and treatment with amoxicillin-clavulanate. Nine days after the first drain persistent symptoms led to infectious disease consultation, piperacillin/tazobactam and vancomycin, a second image-guided drainage and then laparoscopic ileocecectomy with primary anastomosis, which found additional perforations and multiple small abscesses. Infection signs abated and she was discharged on oral metronidazole.

Later visits included a Crohn flare concern with infliximab continued, admission with acute elbow and knee pain treated with daptomycin, ertapenem and micafungin, and a third IR drain placed at a separate hospital. Two months after the initial encounter she presented with fever, abdominal pain and non-bloody diarrhea, and diagnostic laparoscopy for concern of recurrent fistula found dense adhesions and a recurrent psoas abscess.

The abscess was unroofed, irrigated, debrided and packed with an omental flap. She recovered well and was discharged four days later on oral antibiotics, and ultrasound two months later showed the abscess had healed with no drainable fluid. To date she remains symptom-free on biologic therapy with no abscess recurrence.
